summary: Linear search checks items one at a time. Binary search halves a sorted list on each step, so it needs far fewer comparisons on long lists.
notes: mid = (low + high) // 2 uses // so mid is an int. A single / gives a float and items[mid] raises TypeError.
low = mid + 1 and high = mid - 1 skip mid, because it was already checked.
Both functions return a tuple (index, comparisons). -1 means not found.
pitfall: Running binary search on an unsorted list gives wrong answers with no error, often -1 for a value that is in the list.
